pairs: Et vidi cælum novum et terram novam.
I saw the new heaven and the new earth.
Primum enim cælum, et prima terra abiit,
For the first heaven and the first earth passed away,
and the sea is no more.
Et ego Joannes vidi sanctam civitatem Jerusalem novam descendentem de cælo a Deo, paratam sicut sponsam ornatam viro suo.
And I, John, saw the Holy City, the New Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God, prepared like a bride adorned for her husband.
Et audivi vocem magnam de throno dicentem:
And I heard a great voice from the throne, saying:
“Behold the tabernacle of God with men.
And he will dwell with them,
and they will be his people.
et ipse Deus cum eis erit eorum Deus:
And God himself will be their God with them.
et absterget Deus omnem lacrimam ab oculis eorum:
And God will wipe away every tear from their eyes.
And death shall be no more.
For the first things have passed away.”
Et dixit qui sedebat in throno:
And the One who was sitting upon the throne, said,
quia hæc verba fidelissima sunt, et vera.
for these words are entirely faithful and true.”
I am the Alpha and the Omega,
Ego sitienti dabo de fonte aquæ vitæ,
I will give freely from the fountain of the water of life.
Whoever prevails shall possess these things.
And I will be his God,
and he shall be my son.
pars illorum erit in stagno ardenti igne et sulphure:
these shall be a part of the pool burning with fire and sulphur,
Et venit unus de septem angelis habentibus phialas plenas septem plagis novissimis,
And one of the seven Angels, those holding the bowls filled with the seven last afflictions,
and I will show you the bride,
Et sustulit me in spiritu in montem magnum
And he took me up in spirit to a great and high mountain.
And he showed me the Holy City Jerusalem,
et ostendit mihi civitatem sanctam Jerusalem descendentem de cælo a Deo,
descending out of heaven from God,
et lumen ejus simile lapidi pretioso tamquam lapidi jaspidis,
And its light was like that of a precious stone,
even like that of the jasper stone or like crystal.
And at the gates were twelve Angels.
And names were written upon them,
quæ sunt nomina duodecim tribuum filiorum Israël:
which are the names of the twelve tribes of the sons of Israel.
On the East were three gates,
and on the North were three gates,
and on the South were three gates,
and on the West were three gates.
Et murus civitatis habens fundamenta duodecim,
And the wall of the City had twelve foundations.
et in ipsis duodecim nomina duodecim apostolorum Agni.
And upon them were the twelve names of the twelve Apostles of the Lamb.
Et qui loquebatur mecum, habebat mensuram arundineam auream,
And he who was speaking with me was holding a golden measuring reed,
in order to measure the City,
Et civitas in quadro posita est,
And the city is laid out as a square,
et longitudo ejus tanta est quanta et latitudo:
and so its length is as great as the width.
et mensus est civitatem de arundine aurea per stadia duodecim millia:
And he measured the city with the golden reed for twelve thousand stadia,
Et mensus est murum ejus centum quadraginta quatuor cubitorum,
And he measured its wall as one hundred and forty-four cubits,
Et erat structura muri ejus ex lapide jaspide:
And the structure of its wall was of jasper stone. Yet truly,
ipsa vero civitas aurum mundum simile vitro mundo.
the city itself was of pure gold, similar to pure glass.
Et fundamenta muri civitatis omni lapide pretioso ornata.
And the foundations of the wall of the city were adorned with every kind of precious stone.
The first foundation was of jasper,
Et duodecim portæ, duodecim margaritæ sunt,
And the twelve gates are twelve pearls,
et singulæ portæ erant ex singulis margaritis:
so that each gate was made from a single pearl.
And the main street of the city was of pure gold,
Et templum non vidi in ea:
And I saw no temple in it.
Dominus enim Deus omnipotens templum illius est,
For the Lord God Almighty is its temple,
Et civitas non eget sole neque luna ut luceant in ea,
And the city has no need of sun or moon to shine in it.
For the glory of God has illuminated it,
and the Lamb is its lamp.
Et ambulabunt gentes in lumine ejus:
And the nations shall walk by its light.
et reges terræ afferent gloriam suam et honorem in illam.
And the kings of the earth shall bring their glory and honor into it.
Et portæ ejus non claudentur per diem:
And its gates shall not be closed throughout the day,
for there shall be no night in that place.
Et afferent gloriam et honorem gentium in illam.
And they shall bring the glory and honor of the nations into it.
Non intrabit in eam aliquod coinquinatum,
There shall not enter into it anything defiled,
nisi qui scripti sunt in libro vitæ Agni.
but only those who have been written in the Book of Life of the Lamb.
